The branch references supplied prior wording for Employee mobile, Payroll, Employee web, Rondo, Owner, Settings, and Reports. The Timecards and Screens references supplied screen context. The available Spanish report was `es-rest.md`, including its Reports and Premium notes. The live Insights screen is `src/components/reports.tsx` on this base.

The English comes from the current component or route at the cited source line. JSX entities use their rendered characters. Interpolation uses named braces, and adjacent copy separated by a link or emphasis stays in separate keys. There are 343 keys for singular or plural variants. Existing shell, receipt and Payroll import tables are already on the base. Legal documents, UI preview, native app files, and server action messages are outside this review.

3,074 pairs used an on-device translation draft. Glossary checks and targeted edits covered common labels, higher-risk instructions, and selected phone strings. The draft still needs an editorial pass in context during wiring.

Instructions for third-party menus keep the specific menu labels used in the prior Spanish copy, including Agregar calendario in Outlook.

### Strings to resolve during wiring

- Dates, times and amounts that arrive as variables need formatting at the caller. Use the existing Puerto Rico Spanish formatters where they fit. Confirm `6:00 a. m. – 2:00 p. m.`, `7–13 dic`, `lun 23 nov`, and `$1,234.56`.
- Server-projected data includes user-written titles, messages and names. Reports and Rondo can also receive English definitions, observation notes and answers from data sources. The source line that renders those values has no local English literal to extract.
- Keep CSV headers and other file-format values as specified by their import contracts. Use localized labels when the screen needs to explain them.
- The source scan and the locale tests check table structure. Claude verifies visible states, composed fragments, and one-line actions on the wired 390 px screens.

Every selected literal has a table entry.

### Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` passed.
- `npx oxlint` passed with four warnings also present on the base.
- `npm test -- copy.test.ts --maxWorkers 4` passed all 531 tests, including the 426 new table tests.
- The source audit reconciled all 8,712 English entries with the selected source text and line references, checked the named placeholders and glossary terms, and confirmed that the diff contains tables, their tests, and this report. `git diff --check` passed.
- `npm test -- --maxWorkers 6` reported 16,684 passed, 1 failed, and 1,000 skipped. `src/test/manual-publication.test.ts` reported “Stale or foreign application content hash”. The untouched base reproduced the same single failure, with 16,258 passed and 1,000 skipped.
- Claude owns wiring and browser verification, including the one-line check at 390 px.

## Phase 2 Spanish review — Portal & Account

The draft is local in `/Users/josek0514/.codex/worktrees/nevora-spanish-phase-2`, detached from `claude-codex-collab-nevora` at `8c6ee1b67fd987189bd7edbe6d68655c2aaff036`. The translation tables are wired in this local preview so Jose can review the actual screens. There are no Phase 2 commits, pushes, merges, or deployments.

### Areas

| Area | Signed-in surfaces |
| --- | --- |
| Home | Employee, Lead, company Manager, location Manager, Who’s working, Hours this week, Activity. The Owner ready-state comparison is in Phase 1. |
| Portal | More, Notifications, Things to do, Requests hub, Updates, Update detail, Compose, Help, restricted access, missing page, Time off. |
| Account | Employee, Lead, and Manager variants of Profile, Calendar, Device Alerts, Passkeys, Account Deletion. The Owner ready-state Profile comparison is in Phase 1. |

[Spanish Review dashboard](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#route-1)

### Wording decisions

- Jose selected `Empleado` for the person-plus shortcut on Owner and Company Manager Home. Its accessible description is `Añadir empleado`. The shortcut opens the new employee form.
- Jose selected `Cubrir` for the coverage button in Pendientes.
- The Spanish Profile language hint describes the saved account preference. Claude’s original English hint says “Sign-in pages only” and is retained for review under the exact-English rule.
- The selected Owner Home date format remains “Martes, 24 Noviembre”. Short calendar dates and ranges on other surfaces use Puerto Rico Spanish.
- Use `Días libres`, `Pendientes`, `Avisos`, `Localidades`, and `Configuración` for the destinations. Use `Marcación` for the clock record and `Marcar entrada` for the action.
- The calendar integration uses `enlace privado`. Passkeys use `llaves de acceso` in the account drafts.
- Linked legal and policy bodies retain their source language. Names, published notice titles and bodies, employee-entered request reasons, and unrecognized server messages retain the text people or the server supplied.

### Review evidence

- The Owner and Company Manager employee shortcut preserves its spacing at all five widths and both text sizes in Chromium and WebKit. The dashboard shows the confirmed visual defects still open on these pages. [Compare the Home revisions](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#route-1)
- Compared 17 routes and 33 role or view variants at 390 px and 1440 px using the exact collab English checkout and the local Spanish draft. Both production-mode previews used disposable local PostgreSQL and matched fictional fixtures.
- The 66 viewport pairs matched on visible heading font family, size and weight, and on the visible SVG size and viewBox sequence. CSS and the shared Direction B kit have zero diff. The sampled action labels fit on one line at 390 px. Hours this week measured 2 px of horizontal overflow in both languages. Screenshots can show differences in line wrapping and live timestamps.
- The stored Profile language choice survived navigation. Keyboard navigation from Requests opened the Spanish time-off form. The board rendered both images for the selected Manager view and kept the two Phase 1 approvals.
- Device Alerts and Passkeys were captured in their local unavailable states. Reuse the account tests for the alternate controller states. The comparison review does not cover native device enrollment, outbound notifications, or a live account deletion.
- Type checking and Oxlint passed. The final targeted run passed 290 tests across 55 files. An initial full run on the in-progress draft did not pass. The rerun of its four other affected test files passed 44 of 45 tests on the final draft and 45 of 45 against clean collab. The remaining failure is the published-manual application-content fingerprint, which still names the collab snapshot.

#### Wording and fit review

The Home coverage row uses “Cubrir turno” for one and “Cubrir turnos” for several. The document follows the saved profile language using the language provider approved in Phase 3.

The Home coverage button says “Cubrir.” Its accessible name includes the shift. The next shift retains “hoy” when it falls today.

When the open-shifts figure cannot fit “Turnos disponibles,” it shows “Sin cubrir.” Its accessible name includes the full term and count.

The add-shift shortcut shows “Turno” when “Añadir turno” does not fit. Its accessible name retains the full action. The coverage row allows the complete shift time on enlarged text.

The 23 Schedule and Team pages now use the signed-in person’s saved language in the isolated review worktree. Claude’s collab reference is `8c6ee1b67fd987189bd7edbe6d68655c2aaff036`. The Team changes cover the roster and attendance filters, adding or importing employees, the employee profile, pay rate, scheduling restrictions, time-off balance, Clocker PIN and sign-in assistance.

Jose approved “Disponibles”, “4 disp.” and “11 pers.” in the compact weekly grid, “Sin marcar” in the Team filter, “ID con foto” for the sign-in verification method, the shift-change warning, and tú on the PIN page. English control positions and dimensions matched their original measurements in all eight configurations. #### Verification and custody

TypeScript passed. Oxlint exited successfully with four warnings. The local copy suite passed 202 tests in 152 files. The production-build QA clone matched all 514 changed source and test files. Its serial full-suite rerun passed 16,620 tests, with zero failures and 1,000 skips. In the uncommitted worktree, the manual-publication test still reports a stale application content hash for the checked-in guides. The source-qualified manuals were generated only in the disposable clone.

The interactive dashboard contains 1,114 pairs and 510 unmasked English pixel diffs. All 23 page selectors, both images in every pair, and the four review actions were verified. Jose’s individual approvals are recorded on their page revisions. The dashboard records his phase-wide visual approval against each of the 23 reviewed page revisions. Codex’s review worktree remains detached at Claude’s reference `8c6ee1b67`; its index is empty. The harness used only local temporary commits and databases.

#### Shared Manager bell investigation

The English and Spanish Manager bell reads can return HTTP 503. On two separate local fictional databases, the reader exceeded its 1,000,000-byte limit when more notifications became due. One failure measured 1,015,862 bytes across 20 candidates. Schedule reads contributed 554,726 bytes and the shift-maintenance read contributed 406,068 bytes. The browser reproduced the failure after a fresh navigation. All eight reads in a newly seeded Manager session returned HTTP 200. The collab and local service source hashes match. Jose chose to track a shared-service fix separately from Phase 3. The local investigation made no product change to the service.

### Impeccable review of the Schedule references

The owned production harness rendered a published week for a fictional Owner, with people, open shifts and missing pay rates. The English source is the collab commit above. The earlier Spanish build is `0ac957ff08d1449f6964a72e169f6ded1e62752b`. Each build used its own throwaway local Postgres and a saved language preference. The gallery has five widths, two text sizes and both browser engines. The 200% setting sets the root font size to 32px.

- **Hierarchy.** At 390 px both references lead with the page title and locality selector, followed by the week, staffing summary and day list.
- **Spacing.** At 768 px the Spanish open-shifts heading is clipped, the count buttons overrun their cells, the weekly total collides with the first day, and the Settings label breaks before its final letter. Inspect the tablet detail in the dashboard.
- **Accessibility.** The table below preserves the harness and axe findings for the reference builds. The harness can count overlapping rectangles in closed disclosures. A flag alone does not establish a visible collision. Glass contrast requires a rendered-pixel check. Full focus order and tap reach require verification on the integrated candidate.
- **States.** The captures cover a populated, published Owner week. Other roles, alternate weeks, open dialogs and empty, error and loading states remain pending.

### Verification of the draft

Both new copy tests passed. The two files contain 190 pairs. TypeScript passed. Repository lint exited successfully with four warnings in pre-existing files. The final full-suite run passed 16,352 tests, with 1,000 skipped and zero failures. An earlier run during the browser work hit an intermittent process-identity assertion in phase-e-fork-birth.test.ts. The affected file passed on its own, then the full suite passed without source changes. The candidate is an uncommitted, detached worktree at the collab revision. The existing Spanish-copy branch and its earlier drafts remain available separately. The dashboard retained its existing review history.

At 768 px in Chromium with default text, “Turnos disponibles” has 129 px of content in an 87 px label. Each “4 disponibles” text run is 81 px wide inside a roughly 67 px button that also contains a chevron. A zero horizontal page-overflow reading did not catch either defect. The grid’s weekly-total text crosses its cell boundary. The tablet detail in the dashboard shows the affected cells beside the English original.

### José’s compact grid wording decision

In a separate local production capture, alternate labels were measured in the existing Chromium controls at 768 px. “Disponibles” measured 79.3 px against the current row label’s 86.5 px allowance. “4 disp.” measured 40.5 px against the 66.7 px day button, with 4 px between the label and chevron. The same button fit “12 disp.” with 1.0 px clearance on the left. “12 libres” exceeded the left edge by 1.1 px. José approved “Disponibles” and “4 disp.” for the weekly grid. For wiring, use gridOpenShifts for the visible row heading and openCountOne/openCountOther for the visible count. Keep openShifts as the accessible row heading and week legend, and preserve the full count and weekday in each button’s spoken label.

The current weekly total “11 personas · 449 h” exceeds the right edge by 10.5 px. “11 pers. · 449 h” measured 98.3 px and left 15.7 px of clearance. José approved the compact total for the visible grid cell. Use gridPeopleOne/gridPeopleOther for the visible text and scheduledPeopleOne/scheduledPeopleOther for its accessible name.

#### Glossary choices and decisions

Use “Aviso de ausencia” for an employee’s call-out, “Líder de turno” for shift lead and “Tarifa por hora” for hourly rate. José approved “ID con foto” for the selected method on Help someone sign in. The option keeps the existing English value used by the verification record. José also approved the Shift changes warning and tú throughout the Clocker PIN page, including “Escríbelo otra vez” and “Díselo en persona”. José approved “Sin marcar” for the attendance filter. Employee rows use “Sin marcar entrada”. Keep the number, a. or p., and m. together with nonbreaking spaces. The workload and open-shift abbreviations approved for the weekly grid apply only there.

#### Integration and strings requiring placement

The two collab production builds have the same commit. The English gallery renders the original. The Spanish gallery first saves the fictional employee’s preference, then applies the draft to text and accessible labels in the browser. These captures rehearse layout. The application still needs its real ES bindings. The earlier screens-final build was scanned separately and supplies translation references.

* The collab document root returns `en` for an authenticated session at `src/app/layout.tsx:44`. The Spanish profile API independently confirms `savedLanguage: es`. The saved-Spanish language gate is open.
* The manager swap warning “Not available under the current rules.” originates in `src/lib/data/shift-changes.ts:1069`. José approved the display text “Las reglas actuales no permiten este cambio.” Bind a presentation label to this outcome. A translated sentence inside the data response would change the contract.
* The account balance dictionary already uses “tiempo libre” in several places. The requested glossary uses “días libres”. Those existing protected entries are listed below for José.
* The standard Owner fixture shows the designed import-unavailable state. Its Manager variant explains Owner access. A second, locally provisioned fictional company exercised the enabled form, validation preview, submission and matching database receipt in Chromium and WebKit, in both languages. The 120 supplemental captures cover these three states at five widths and two text sizes.
* The capture archive includes separate browser outputs for stock clipping, overlap, alignment, off-screen content, contrast and target size. A focused keyboard traversal can move focus outside the app. Captures showing the privacy pause or loading state cannot stand in for the underlying screen.

### Browser evidence for the remaining routes

The draft covers the 22 remaining Schedule and Team routes on Claude’s collab commit `8c6ee1b67fd987189bd7edbe6d68655c2aaff036`. José can review each comparison and save comments on the [local dashboard](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#route-13). The production-build UI acceptance gate remains open.
The English column renders the original product. The Spanish column has a genuinely saved Spanish profile and applies the copy tables to text and accessible names in the browser. Both columns use the collab components, fonts, icons and styles. Claude still needs to bind the tables in the product. A signed-in app document declares English at `src/app/layout.tsx:44`.
### Impeccable audit
**Blocking.** Edit shift at 320 px and 200% text has a verified Spanish-only header collision. In Chromium the ink bounds of “Cancelar” and “Editar turno” intersect by 29 × 35 px. “Editar turno” and “Guardar” intersect by 13 × 35 px. The English header reports zero overlapping pairs in this state. Shortening the title alone to “Editar” or “Turno” still intersects the controls in both browsers. [Compare headers](http://127.0.0.1:4189/assets/phase3-edit-shift-320-large.png).
**Blocking.** Saved Spanish profiles have the wrong document language for a screen reader. The signed-in language needs a product change. Form focus, target reach and cropped content also have open measurements below. Raw overlap flags include text inside closed disclosures. The per-case archive preserves the original scan and the DOM evidence used to identify those. Only visually confirmed cases are described as visible collisions.
**Hierarchy and spacing.** Compare the title, back action and primary action first at enlarged text. The staff-import review preserves that hierarchy on a 390 px phone. Spanish help text wraps under the person’s details and moves the following section down. Controlled EN/ES imports use matching synthetic records and headcounts. [Compare the import review](http://127.0.0.1:4189/assets/phase3-import-review-390.png).
**Wording and control fit.** In both browsers at 390 px, José’s “ID con foto” occupies about 82 of 134 available pixels. The existing option value is `Verified in person with a photo ID.`. [Compare the sign-in help control](http://127.0.0.1:4189/assets/p3-approved-id-con-foto.png).
**Approved Shift changes warning.** At 390 px the English warning takes one line and “Las reglas actuales no permiten este cambio.” takes two. The following action and row move down about one line. The warning and action remain legible. [Compare the warning](http://127.0.0.1:4189/assets/phase3-approved-shift-warning-390.png). [Compare the Clocker PIN instructions](http://127.0.0.1:4189/assets/phase3-approved-clocker-pin-390.png).
**States.** The gallery includes a publish review, an expandable request, a real replacement candidate, a saved copy receipt, shift swap and callout, the second employee-setup step, access, role and position views, a first-run time-off balance and an Owner-restricted importer. The enabled importer ran against disposable, routed workplace databases with real validation and database-verified receipts. No real messages, billing handoff or hosted environment were used. A new template is an inline form on the initial page. Loading captures are excluded from the complete-view count. The gallery does not certify every possible server failure or data combination.

### Time wrapping and Team attendance filters

The earlier comparison replaced the receipt’s nonbreaking spaces with regular spaces and photographed Team before its two attendance reads finished. Both corrections are in the local Spanish review. Claude’s app already keeps each clock time together on the receipt and shows the filters when attendance is ready.

At 320 px and 100% text, James’s time used to leave “m.” on its own line. The updated receipt moves “5:00 p. m.” together. Across Owner and Manager in Chromium and WebKit, all 1,720 measured Spanish times occupied one line per time. This covers all five widths at both text sizes. [Compare the receipt](http://127.0.0.1:4189/assets/receipt-time-wrap-320.png).

Across 40 matched Team comparisons, the four controls, attendance counts, employee identities, per-person attendance states and minutes, and bell state match. José approved “Sin marcar” for the filter. Its employee-row equivalent remains “Sin marcar entrada”. At 390 px and 100% text, all four Spanish labels fit on one line in both browsers. The fixtures were refreshed with the same data in English and Spanish. [Compare Team](http://127.0.0.1:4189/assets/team-filter-bar-390.png).

Axe reported zero violations in the 160 updated Team and receipt views. There were 200 observed filter selections across the two languages. The check compares the resulting employee list in English and Spanish after each selection. [Open the measurements](/Users/josek0514/.codex/visualizations/2026/11/23/01a20955-ae60-7240-883e-23f8782875b5/spanish-review/qa/phase-3/remaining/clock-and-team/correction-results.json).

For Claude’s binding, the receipt already composes the translated suffix in `src/components/copy-receipt-copy.ts:65` with the range spacing in `src/components/copy-receipt.tsx:37`. Preserve those spaces. Render the Team filter labels from the phone and desktop filter tables, and use `team-live-copy.ts` for the full row status. Both existing Team views render the filters once their attendance reads settle.

In the additional Shift changes checks, enlarged-text cells as narrow as 103 px can wrap between the number and its day period. Allow a break before the day period only when the complete timestamp will not fit on one line. Keep U+00A0 between a. or p. and m. The six affected views had zero splits inside the day period. Each measured wrap is recorded in the JSON.

### Strings to verify during wiring

- For date ranges, day names and monetary amounts, pass formatted values in the saved language. Preserve nonbreaking spaces inside each Spanish clock time. Use the approved full-date form (“Martes, 24 Noviembre”) where a full heading is called for, and compact dates such as “7–13 dic” in ranges.
- Check the timecard decision receipts, private pay-statement titles and imported amounts with the same fictional records in each language. Employee and provider data, identifiers and exported file headers keep the values supplied.
- Import payroll, Clocker recovery and the paid-time export route now receive the saved profile language locally.
- Server action messages are outside this pass. A runtime message supplied entirely by a server or browser has no component literal to bind. Record the actual message and state if it appears during the visual audit.

The same return link on Personas and Corregir antes de la nómina uses “Detalles”. At 320 px and 200% text the original Spanish link reached x = 361 on both pages. The destination title is “Detalles de la nómina”.

### Wording and English reference checks

The local dashboard serves one wording revision for each of the 15 pages. It includes 75 full-page English references from the owned production build, at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px. The review dashboard opened all 15 wording sets and their source links in both Chromium and WebKit. The screenshot reader checked the PNG format and width of every reference.

#### Claude’s English scan

Claude’s Chromium audit inspected 130 route and viewport combinations on the English reference. The following are raw detector observations. One element can produce observations at several widths. A report of overlap across closed disclosures needs a visible-state check before classifying it as a design defect.

| Role | Views | Clipped | Off-screen | Overlap | Small targets | Contrast | Row alignment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Owner | 65 | 1 | 0 | 261 | 70 | 345 | 10 |
| Manager | 35 | 1 | 0 | 127 | 70 | 142 | 0 |
| Lead | 15 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 35 | 10 |
| Employee | 15 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 35 | 10 |

The stock late-evening Owner fixture capped two fictional shifts at the same start and end time. In the disposable Owner and Manager scans, the latest start is 22:30 and the latest end is 23:30. All four targeted timecard states rendered for each role. Screenshot capture clears text selection left by the interaction probe. Two fictional pending-correction seeds still failed in the Owner and Manager runs, and one failed in the Employee and Lead runs. Those missing fixture states require a targeted check during Spanish integration.

At 390 px the English Time exports detector reported overlap between “Select all finalized” and “Other dates.” The default screenshot shows the people selector collapsed. The English report also flagged People in this payroll. The expanded rows, focus states, contrast and enlarged text need direct comparison in the final bilingual audit.

#### Initial wording checks

The 67 copy-table tests passed. TypeScript passed. Repository lint exited successfully with four warnings in unchanged files. The unit suite recorded 16,442 passes, 1,000 skips and one failure. The manuals qualification reports “Stale or foreign application content hash” on the untouched collab snapshot as well.

#### Local implementation and visual review

The 15 Phase 4 pages are wired in the isolated review worktree against collab commit `9a5dc76134ee215806e0e85f995f4d3079c6afda`. The dashboard opens each English and Spanish comparison at the selected role, text size, browser and width. The wording history and visual decisions have separate revisions. [Review dashboard](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#route-48)

The review includes 520 full-page comparisons, 40 additional comparisons of the export receipt and empty period, and 16 open timecard and issue comparisons. The saved Spanish profile rendered `lang="es"` in all 520 route captures. Axe reported zero violations in both browsers. The 56 weekly-summary boundary checks verified two rows below 360 px at 200% text and zero changed summary pixels at the default text size. The correction queue buttons retain their padding at 320 px and 200% text.

Across the final code checks, all 68 table files passed their 73 tests, TypeScript passed and lint returned four existing warnings. The full suite recorded 16,454 passes, 1,000 skips and one failure. The checked-in manuals fail the same content hash qualification on the pristine collab commit. The two regression tests for the newly translated export states passed.

The keyboard, hit-target and contrast evidence is retained with the visual report. The desktop sidebar focus indicator is invisible in both languages in the 768 px comparison. The edge of some Timecards name buttons lands on their table cells. Part of the Clocker recovery heading falls inside the Settings back link's hit area in both languages. The shared issues remain in Claude’s handoff for Jose. The local changes await visual approval.

#### Saved export receipt spacing

Flag for Claude’s English UI. In Recent exports, Download CSV and Time record have a 0 px gap at 390 px for Owner and company-wide Manager in Chromium and WebKit. The local Spanish receipt now uses 12 px between buttons in a row, 8 px between stacked buttons, and 8 px below the export metadata. Both actions fit at all five audit widths at 100% and 200% text. Lead and Employee each saw the restricted page. [Side-by-side dashboard](http://127.0.0.1:4189/?review=receipt-spacing#route-48)

#### Wording and fit review

The Spanish payroll totals preview gives the label and amount their own lines when enlarged text needs more room. The approved wording, amount and currency formatting stay together in the same row.

#### Spanish tap targets and English findings for Claude

On Tarjetas de tiempo, 264 Spanish employee-name buttons on Owner and Manager tables passed every edge. The bottom edge opened the correct employee in all 24 table views. The original English layout missed the bottom edge on 39 buttons in Chromium at 200% text. This English finding is open for Claude. [Review the paired screens](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#route-26)

#### November 25 Spanish UI verification

The Spanish “Exportar horas” and “Correcciones de tiempo” links align at 63 px on 320 and 390 px phones using 200% text, for both Owner and Manager. The desktop sidebar also shows keyboard focus. [Local side-by-side review](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#route-26)

#### Clocker back links on November 25

### Glossary choices

The standard place name is “Localidad”. A company that selected a different terminology preset sees its own place name. The Clocker setup path reads “Configuración → Tabletas de Clocker”. Small and Team are billing plan names. “Días libres”, “Horario”, “Configuración de nómina” and “Recuperación de Clocker” follow the earlier reviews.

### Strings and states pending visual placement

The tables cover source wording for page entries, forms, stored settings, client feedback and tablet setup. The local Spanish screens and English comparisons are available on the dashboard. Jose approved the restaurant forms and the singular and plural position counts. The location announcement uses the reviewed “en uso” wording for the company’s chosen place name. The kiosk already has its own bilingual catalogue. Employee-entered names, company-entered assistance instructions, server action responses and legal documents retain their own sources.

The original copy review covered 60 tables. Local integration added the payroll navigation table. All 61 tables have key and placeholder tests. ### Local integration and follow-up decisions

Jose approved the Phase 5 wording and local wiring. Billing starts in the saved profile language. Its language switch applies to the current billing view. The platform’s verified photo-deletion and backup disclosures appear verbatim in Owner settings and on the kiosk. The affected-draft payroll instruction appears in Spanish only when the read response contains the reviewed instruction.

The Clocker tablets status announcement uses “1 conectada” and “1 eliminada”. It uses “conectadas” and “eliminadas” for zero or multiple tablets. Both browsers announced “1 conectada, 1 sin configurar, 0 eliminadas” on the fictional Owner profile at 390 px. The Add location header uses “Volver” when the full destination would overlap “Añadir”. Jose approved the large-text wrapping for the Branding rows. At 320 px, 200% text places “Turquesa” below “Color” and “Ninguna” below “Logo”. Phase 5 visual approval is pending. [Review dashboard](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#route-64)

The PIN filters and row action reflow for enlarged text. The shared tablet shows the full setup path and switches languages from the same button. A 320 px screen shows “Fotos” with a full accessible destination and zero horizontal scroll. For the restaurant preset, forms say “Activo,” “Inactivo” and “No disponible mientras está inactivo.” The positions announcement uses “1 puesto activo y 1 archivado” when both counts are one.

Jose approved this additional payroll draft instruction during local integration. Workplace billing opens in the person’s saved language. Its language switch affects only the billing view. The platform’s verified photo-deletion and backup disclosures are shown as supplied in Settings and on the kiosk.

Jose approved a shorter setup-code button label, “Código,” when “Obtener código” exceeds its column. The button’s accessible name identifies the action and the tablet. He also approved placing the color value and logo status below their labels in Marca when enlarged text needs the space, and using the singular verb in “La configuración de nómina forma parte de Configuración.”

The Break types announcement uses “Se muestra” for one shown and “Se muestran” for zero or more than one. The restricted Settings heading can break “Configuración” at a Spanish syllable at enlarged text sizes for Managers, Leads and Employees. The full accessible names remain available when the Photo review back link uses “Fotos” or the PIN directory search field shows “Buscar”. Jose approved the PIN-directory and tablet-setup wrapping, including the directory’s third filter when an employee is inactive.

#### Short labels and whole words

The Settings list uses “Tabletas” under Clocker and “Nómina” under pay. The statement-language summary reads “Idioma.” In a narrow sidebar, “Ajustes” opens Configuración. The accessible name includes both words. The location list counts eligible people as “1 persona” and “11 personas.” Zero uses “0 personas.” The destination still uses the company’s selected term for its locations.

### Source content and display rules

- Use the saved profile language for interface text and the signed-in document. The static route metadata, loading announcements and error actions have separate entries.
- Personal names, original file contents, saved notes and generated answers retain their source language.
- Rondo and Insights receive free-text attention notes, report definitions, overtime explanations and clock-in observations from their read responses. Their English has no component literal. The local tables cover the fixed labels. The displayed report language and the independently selected period-review language are separate.
- Preserve the operation codes, CSV column identifiers and stored request language. Wire the dynamic day and time values through the existing display formatters.

### Verification

- 28 bilingual tables contain 1,462 pairs. The sensitive wording table contains 595 rows. Earlier reviews contain 121 matching English labels. The candidate aligns 20 entries with those decisions.
- The 16 approved Rondo phrases are presentation-only translations for known source text. New, unmatched source text and workplace names keep their supplied wording.
- Chromium and WebKit captured 260 of 260 applicable Spanish views. The dashboard has 260 side-by-side comparisons. The four profiles include Owner, Manager, Lead and Employee. Restricted profiles show the access explanation for reports.
- The saved Spanish profile uses a Spanish document language. Both browsers show “Comparar” at 320 px and 200% text and expose “Comparar opciones” to screen readers. The weekly source text fits without splitting words in all 20 measured views. All 40 bonus views show “Fecha de pago” and the full date range.
- The Informes phone filters separate wrapped touch targets by the existing 8 px spacing token. Enlarged planned hours, overtime, the card label and the annual-report description wrap.
- Full suite ran with 16,519 passed, 0 failed and 1,000 skipped. TypeScript, oxlint and all 28 table checks passed. Lint reported four warnings.

The daily-hours chart uses the approved initials L, M, X, J, V, S and D when the three-letter day labels would touch. Both roles and both browsers used initials at 320 and 390 px with 200% text and returned to the abbreviations at 430 px. All 48 chart checks preserved the seven dates and kept visible labels apart.

Across 130 default-size English comparisons, the position and size of inspected controls and cards matched in 130. Full image heights matched. 105 had zero changed pixels above the tolerance. The remaining images have small differences in painted content, such as the header controls or live report figures.

The [browser evidence and Impeccable review](http://127.0.0.1:4189/#p6-audit) gives the counts, actual comparisons, limitations and outstanding findings. Local review precedes any commit.

The Phase 7 dashboard lists one route, `/pages/plans`. The source is collab `6983360dd74c0ce51ef62d2fbdab3284c983ebd5`. The local Spanish page is ready for visual review.

### Terminology and source content

Jose chose **Admin** for this public sign-in instruction. The permission remains Owner. The existing NEVORA wordmark and “Powered by VELANI LLC” credit follow DESIGN.MD. The legal footer identifies its existing English ownership sentence with `lang="en"`. All four changed strings are accounted for.

### Local verification

Claude’s archived public harness does not list this route. The disposable harness copy adds it to the public scan. All checks ran over the owned HTTPS loopback origin using a throwaway PostgreSQL database. The two public states are sign-in required and billing unavailable. No billing handoff was pressed. Authenticated Stripe or payment states are outside this public-page review.

Chromium and WebKit each checked 20 Spanish and 20 English views at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px with 100% and 200% text. On Spanish each browser checked 480 tap points and 120 focus stops. Both recorded zero unresolved clipping, overlap, off-screen text, tap misses, axe violations or console errors. “Iniciar sesión” fit on one line in all 40 Spanish views. The browser title, description and document language followed both directions of the language switch. Four additional checks confirmed first-visit Spanish metadata with JavaScript disabled.

All 20 default-size English image pairs had equal dimensions and 19 were pixel-identical. In the Chromium 390 px sign-in capture, the remaining 13 pixels were at the left edge of the language switch at x=195–200, y=34–39. Two crossed the eight-level channel threshold. The keyboard walk used Tab in Chromium and macOS Option–Tab in WebKit to include links. The smallest measured contrast on the unselected language switch was 4.52∶1. TypeScript, oxlint and the focused tests passed. The full test suite recorded 16,425 passed, 0 failed and 1,000 skipped.
